hypotheses.H1: Rank aggregation combined with selection stability produces more stable feature subsets than individual feature-selection methods, while maintaining comparable downstream predictive performance under a fixed-model comparison.
hypotheses.H0: The proposed approach does not produce a meaningful improvement in feature-selection stability without unacceptable predictive-performance degradation.

baselines.description: Uses 100% of available features without filtering.
Mean Decrease in Impurity (MDI) feature importances.
Permutation feature importance evaluated on validation folds.
Recursive feature elimination with reference estimator.

proposed.description: Ensemble rank aggregation combining 4 normalized base selectors.
Ensemble rank aggregation weighted with cross-fold selection stability (alpha=0.7 / alpha=0.5).

anti_leakage_invariants: Development vs Locked Test outer split occurs strictly before any modeling or selection.
Feature selectors and transformers are fit strictly inside individual training fold slices.
Selection stability S(j) is computed strictly across repeated CV runs on the Development partition.
Locked Test partition is evaluated at most once per proposed method and never by baselines.
Downstream reference estimator is fixed across all compared methods (ADR-014).

statistical_evaluation_criteria.primary_comparison: Fixed-model controlled comparison between Experiment B (RANK_AGGREGATION_STABILITY), Experiment A (RANK_AGGREGATION), and individual baselines.
paired_tests: Wilcoxon signed-rank test across paired fold metrics
statistical_evaluation_criteria.stability_metric: Selection frequency S(j) = (count of selections) / (total runs)
statistical_evaluation_criteria.reporting_scope: Framed as 'across the evaluated benchmark datasets and protocol', without post-hoc generalization claims.
